Waypoints.Name: HCC1143 triple negative breast cancer cell line
Waypoints.Description: The IMC study profiled the triple-negative breast cancer cell line HCC1143 to analyze tumor differentiation and invasiveness. Using multiple markers in a single assay, researchers successfully identified key cellular traits: a mesenchymal shape with high cytoplasmic vimentin, nuclear p53, cytoplasmic cytokeratin 5, and active cell division via Ki-67.

Waypoints.Name: Sample Preparation
Waypoints.Description: A specialized immunocytostaining workflow for cultured cell monolayers on slides was developed, using isotopically enriched, cell-line-specific antibody panels and DNA nuclear labeling reagents for high-dimensional imaging mass cytometry (IMC). This method encompasses live-cell S-phase and viability staining, surface/intracellular marker antibody staining, fixation, and validation against proteomic databases for the Hyperion Imaging System.

Waypoints.Name: Sample Acquisition
Waypoints.Description: Samples were analyzed using the Hyperion Imaging System, where UV laser ablation of selected ROIs on cell-line slides generated aerosol plumes that were transferred to a CyTOF Helios instrument for detection. To ensure statistically relevant analysis without biological replicates, a cellular seeding density of 0.25 × 10⁶ per well was utilized to collect at least 1,000 cells per experiment, with data stored in MCD format.

Waypoints.Name: Qualitative analysis
Waypoints.Description: To perform qualitative pseudo-color imaging analysis, 32-bit single-channel TIFF images were exported from MCD/txt files via MCD Viewer. These images were processed in CellProfiler 4.2.4 using sequential modules to rescale, clip, smooth with a gaussian filter, and combine gray channels into 16-bit, multi-color composite images (3 or 4 channels). Markers like DNA-Ir193 (nuclei), pan-keratin/EGFR/vimentin (cytoplasm), and Ki-67 (proliferation) ) were utilized. Finally, subcellular resolution (1 um per pixel) was assessed using ImageJ by cropping zoomed-in regions without changing the pixel size.
